title: Crash Detector private envelope
description: CLOSED. BLUEPRINT §3, §4 and §8. The other side of the hard public/private split (PID doctrine §3.5): a SEPARATE document, validated against a SEPARATE schema, written to a separate table, read by a separate role, served from a separate container on a separate network. This schema is closed for the same reason the public one is, but against a different failure: on the public surface an unknown key is a leak, and here an unknown key is an unaudited field on the side of the boundary where the book lives. Note what this document does NOT do. It does not carry a superset flag, an include_private toggle, or any switch that would let one builder emit either envelope. Two envelopes, two builders, two schemas: a shared builder with a mode parameter is one bug away from emitting the private shape onto the public surface, and 'not the same container, let alone the same page' is not satisfied by 'the same function with a different argument'. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND OWED. The book-adjacent content itself. Which private fields exist, what they mean and which of them a drill-down may show are product decisions this seat has not been given and must not invent (PBG-AUTH-005); CD-AC-006's enforcement evidence is sequenced at WO-5 (CD-D-004, BLUEPRINT §13). WO-2 therefore ships the private envelope with the same honesty fields and the same two dials as the public one, plus its classification. That is the doctrinally correct empty state, and it is the same posture as the empty source registry: the boundary is built now, the content arrives when the Product Owner has ruled on it, and each addition is a deliberate allowlist edit with a schema_version bump.

classification.description: Required and pinned. A private envelope that does not say so cannot be written, so a document cannot arrive at the private table having lost the one label that says where it may go. The public schema declares no classification property at all, so a private envelope validated against the public schema is rejected on this key before anything else about it is considered.

regime.description: As in the public envelope: a non-empty string, deliberately not an enumeration, because naming the regimes is product meaning owed with CD-AC-009 in WO-3.

utc_timestamp.description: ISO-8601, UTC, with an explicit Z. Enforced by pattern, not by format: format is an annotation by default and an annotation is not a refusal.

dial_reading.description: Identical in shape to the public envelope's dial_reading, and duplicated here rather than referenced across files on purpose: a cross-document $ref would make the private contract depend on resolving the public one, and a schema that must fetch another schema to judge a document is a schema with an availability failure mode.
